abstract: Vitamin D supplementation significantly decreases depressive symptoms in adults with deficiency. In a randomized controlled trial, the treatment group showed a 30% reduction in PHQ-9 scores compared to placebo.
Vitamin D supplementation increases depressive symptoms in elderly patients. The study found a 15% increase in PHQ-9 scores in the treatment arm versus control.
Aerobic exercise improves cognitive function in older adults. Participants showed significant gains in executive function and memory after 6 months.
Aerobic exercise has no effect on cognitive function in older adults. No significant differences were found between exercise and control groups on any cognitive measure.
Caffeine consumption increases anxiety levels in sensitive individuals. Doses above 200mg significantly elevated state anxiety scores.
Caffeine consumption decreases anxiety in habitual users. Regular coffee drinkers showed lower baseline anxiety compared to non-drinkers.
Mindfulness meditation reduces perceived stress in healthcare workers. The intervention group reported a 25% reduction in PSS scores.
Mindfulness meditation has no effect on perceived stress in healthcare workers. Both groups showed similar PSS scores at follow-up.
Evening screen time decreases sleep quality in adolescents. Blue light exposure delayed melatonin onset by 45 minutes.
Evening screen time has no effect on sleep quality when controlling for content type. Interactive vs passive use was the key moderator.
Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation improves cardiovascular outcomes. Meta-analysis showed a 10% reduction in major adverse cardiac events.
Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation has no effect on cardiovascular outcomes. The largest trial found no significant benefit over placebo.
Sugar consumption increases hyperactivity in children. Double-blind challenge showed significant behavioral changes after sucrose vs placebo.
Sugar consumption has no effect on hyperactivity in children. Multiple controlled studies failed to find any behavioral difference.
Remote work increases productivity for knowledge workers. Output metrics rose 13% in the first year of mandatory remote work.
Remote work decreases productivity for collaborative tasks. Team-based projects showed 20% longer completion times.
Vitamin D levels are associated with depressive symptoms. Cross-sectional analysis found a correlation of r=-0.32 between serum 25(OH)D and PHQ-9.
Exercise frequency is linked to cognitive function. Observational data showed a positive association between weekly exercise and MoCA scores.
Vitamin D supplementation may decrease depressive symptoms. The findings suggest a potential benefit but confidence intervals include the null.
Vitamin D supplementation might increase depressive symptoms in some subgroups. The data hint at a possible adverse effect in elderly males.
